Extra read-only folders you may use: handoff-docs, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fqq-Desktop-Topflightapps-roundai/2a408671-6ff1-4104-9d24-9f97da7d0ee6/scratchpad/cr/review-evidence

Scenario TC-04/S10 — How long an unassigned and an assigned box stay on the pad (12 / 18 / 36 h ± 1 h)

Requirements it checks:
- U4: An unassigned box stays on the pad after Quick Dictation is closed and reopened, as the physician's own log. Boxes are never silently dropped. (The UAT says 'stays on the sheet'; the Rounding Sheet is hidden, so we read it as the pad — Q14.)

Given: One unassigned and one assigned box created at T
When: Age the boxes to T+11 h, T+13 h, T+17 h, T+19 h, T+35 h, T+37 h on the server clock, and set the device clock wrong by a day
Then: Boxes stay or clear exactly at the window Q6 settles on, never silently before it, and the same on every device clock
Oracle: U4 (never silently dropped) against the window Daniela gives for Q6; 3.6 has no row for boxes, so the expected window is unknown today. 3.8: server clock, not device clock

THE ORACLE WINS. The question below only scopes this scenario to what code can decide. If the question, or its pass/fail rule, ever reads differently from the Then/Oracle above, follow the Then/Oracle, give the verdict the oracle gives, and say where they differ in openQuestions.

Open questions the oracle defers to, with the oracle's default for each (do not settle them yourself):
- pending:Q6 — oracle: "against the window Daniela gives for Q6; 3.6 has no row for boxes, so the expected window is unknown today". Default: the window boxes should clear at is unknown until Q6: record what window the code has (or that it has none) under openQuestions and label that finding half:Q6 window; it does not decide this verdict

Gaps the matrix already records (use the id in a label only when the finding is exactly that gap):
- (none)

YOUR QUESTION (answer this, from the code):
Find every code path that deletes or hides a quickDictationDrafts box (unassigned or assigned): a cron (convex/crons.ts), a lifecycle sweep (convex/lib/lifecycle.ts and its callers), a client purge, a TTL, or an explicit user action. For each, which clock does it use (server time or the device clock) and which window? Is there any retention window for boxes at all, and if so what is its value?

pass = no box is removed silently: a box goes only by an explicit user action, or by a rule on the server clock (never the device clock)
fail = a box is dropped silently (no user action removes it, yet it goes), or the rule that clears boxes uses the device clock, not the server clock

Other halves of this scenario that another lane or a person runs (do not judge them; if the code you read predicts one of them, report that as a finding labelled half:<name>, supports = pass or fail):
- half:Q6 window — pending Q6 (Daniela): "Boxes stay or clear exactly at the window Q6 settles on"
- half:ageing run — TIME (T+11..37 h on a moved server clock): "the same on every device clock"

Not part of this verdict (other scenarios, or notes that decide nothing here):
- (none)



Label every finding:
- new: a failing point the matrix does not already record (supports = fail)
- known:<id>: exactly one of the recorded gaps listed above
- pending:<id>: a failing point whose verdict the oracle hands to one of the open questions above
- half:<name>: a point about one of the other halves above
- context: background, not for or against the verdict

Answer with: verdict (pass | fail | pending | unsure), answer (a short paragraph a QA lead can read: what the code does and why that is the verdict; name the recorded gaps and open questions it touches), findings (each with claim, file, line, quote, supports = pass | fail | context, label), physicianImpact, openQuestions, notDecidableByCode.
note: stdout is redacted (lib.mjs redactAll) before it is written; a run whose stdout held secret-like text not in the prompt is not written (stdout null, kinds in withheld)
